question: Does one of the two reviewed experiments independently prepare both R-581 states and read the same order population under the same post-preparation dynamics?
classification: Literature-only applicability audit; no new theorem, experimental result or direction-control admission.
model: Original finite side-16 periodic three-torus, fixed Fourier K/2K for each K>=1, canonical dimensionless tau. At q=Qbar/V=43/432, r=q, a^2=q-r^2, Psi_A=a(1,i,0), Psi_B=a(i,1,0), chi_A=chi_B=r. Same H,Q, populations and Z=0, opposite initial curvature of Npsi under the pinned law. Npsi is the integral of the sum of squared order-component magnitudes, not a single spin fraction, energy current or conserved constituent count. This is the existing R-581 witness only.

sources.source: Blasing et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 073202 (2018), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.073202
sources.locator: https://arxiv.org/html/1807.11608v3 ; Fig. 1, Eqs. (1)-(3), apparatus description before Eq. (2)
sources.native_procedure: Raman dressing prepares an atomic spin-momentum superposition. Pair paths couple to one excited molecular level; spin-resolved absorption imaging counts remaining atoms after photoassociation.
sources.unmet: The common molecular level is a reaction output, not a documented nonzero reservoir coherently prepared in both initial samples. Spontaneous-emission-dominated atom loss has no calibrated mapping here to the reversible EXCH order population. This does not rule out a basis correspondence of pair amplitudes.

sources.source: Chang et al., Nature Physics 1, 111-116 (2005), DOI 10.1038/nphys153
sources.native_procedure: Microwave preparation and imposed phase shifts control a spin-1 condensate. Separated spin populations are imaged. The native process redistributes atom pairs between spin components.
sources.unmet: Figure 3b fits the unknown initial spinor phase in the trajectory reconstruction. A controlled phase shift is not independent certification of both starting phases relative to a common nonzero reservoir. Spin redistribution is not a calibrated change in total Npsi.

decision: Neither protocol establishes both preparation and readout in one apparatus. Do not combine them. No data extraction, fitting, held-out window selection or experimental sign test was performed. This documentary HOLD does not alter R-581's DISPROVED verdict on universal exact reduced drift.
reentry: One independently documented native preparation/readout packet (or an identifiable error in this crosswalk): certify both preparation classes up to the common weighted phase, shared reservoir and coupling orientation, unchanged subsequent law within error, and a common calibrated Npsi readout. Only then freeze an unused finite window before testing signs, including preparation-induced initial slope, timing, loss/detector error and higher-order remainder. No claim of experimental impossibility, unique TECT evidence, Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity or a limit.
